newsitem.title: PERU: IMF to help if Peru has problems paying debt - govt.
newsitem.headline: IMF to help if Peru has problems paying debt - govt.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) would help Peru pay its bank creditors should problems arise in servicing the country's debt, according to the government daily El Peruano's Tuesday edition.

Based on comments by IMF general secretary, Leo van Houtven during a visit to Lima, El Peruano said, "In the case of any difficulty in the period when Peru is paying off its debt with the international banking community, this world organization will contribute to resolving the problem."
The report did not specify how the IMF might help Peru.

El Peruano reported van Houtven as saying the IMF was "not worried" Peru might fail to make its rising debt payments in coming years "because we expect the country to improve its position with the international banking community by refinancing its debt in December."

Last week, Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Reuters the government expected to close its Brady debt restructuring deal with creditor banks in December. The accord would mean reducing the debt included in the deal to $4.604 billion from $10.657 billion, according to Camet.

The Brady accord and a restructuring deal struck earlier this year with the Paris Club of rich-nation creditors mean the government is set to have a new total medium- and long-term debt of $21.258 billion, according to government officials.
Economists estimate the government's combined debt payments will cost a total of more than $1.2 billion next year, rising steeply to between $2 billion and $3 billion by early next century.
The high cost of this debt servicing has prompted some analysts to question whether the economy will grow steadily enough to generate sufficient export income to meet the payments.
Opposition parties also claim the government is neglecting its social programs to finance the country's foreign debt.
